useFor: The shell every page of the app sits in: a sidebar, a topbar and one scrolling page, or the reduced shells for sign-in and the steps before a workspace.

combineWith.how: In the .sidebar, the first child of .layout: the brand, the links and the tools at its foot.
The .topbar is the first child of .content, above .page: the search, the status and the user widget.
The first child of .page, so every page starts with its title and the actions for the whole page.
Between the .topbar and .page, for a notice about the whole app.
The last child of .content, in the sidebar's place below 560px with .layout--bottombar.
The finished pages for each shell: not found keeps .layout, the rest are .auth-layout.

useFor: Moving between the app's pages from the sidebar: links with icons and counts, the current page marked, groups that fold, and a rail of icons.

combineWith.how: The .nav goes in the .sidebar under the brand, with .nav-tools at its foot.
A .topbar-btn--start at the start of the header collapses the sidebar to its rail and expands it again.
On the collapsed rail a link's data-tip becomes a CSS flyout; the bubble itself is skipped inside .sidebar.
When one list holds too many pages, the same links go into accordion groups, a filtered nav or an area rail.

useFor: Arranging a sidebar that has outgrown one list: text-only sections, accordion groups, a filter over the links, or one nav per area chosen from a rail or the header.

combineWith.how: Every layout is built from the same .nav-link rows, so a link moves between them unchanged.
ActiveLink marks the current link, and an area's link by the prefix its pages share.
Areas in the header are .topbar-nav links at the start of the topbar, with the sidebar listing the current area's pages.
On a phone the bar holds the places used most and a sheet holds the whole nav.

notFor.text: A nav short enough to read in one list
Switching between views of the same content
Finding a page, a record or a command by typing

useFor: Moving between the few places used most, or acting on the record in view, with a thumb on a phone.

combineWith.how: With .layout--flow the document scrolls on a phone and the bar sticks to the bottom of the viewport.
The --start cell opens every page in a sheet that holds an ordinary .nav.
Its items are the sidebar's places, and the current one is marked aria-current the same way.
The .bottombar-accessory above the items holds something running in the background, with its progress.
While the bar shows, toasts and a .fab rise above it by its height.

notFor.text: Navigation on a wide screen
Every page of a large app
One action floating over the page
A bar of the app's own along the bottom edge

useFor: The header across every page: the search over the whole app, the app's status and version, a way to other apps, and the signed-in user with their menu.

combineWith.how: The .topbar is the first child of .content, above .page and beside the sidebar.
The user widget opens the library's one dropdown, .menu, under its trigger.
The app switcher is a popover opened by a .topbar-btn with popovertarget.
The status in the right cluster is a .health-badge, its state in a word beside the dot.
The bell is a .topbar-btn whose label carries the unread count, opening the inbox.
An icon-only .topbar-btn is named by aria-label and says its consequence in a data-tip.

combineWith.how: Where the app redirects rather than staying open, the session-expired page takes over from the strip.
Written once in the host page, outside the layout, so it shows over whichever shell the page uses.

useFor: A notice about the whole app under the topbar: a maintenance window, an outage, the phase a service is in, an action that ended on another page, and the cookie choice.

combineWith.how: A sibling of .topbar and .page in .content or .bare-layout, so the page scrolls below it.
Its actions are .btn--sm buttons in .page-banner-actions; the cookie choice puts them in a row under the words.
The phase banner leads with a .badge naming the phase.

useFor: Saying in one line what a control does, or what a mark or a cut-off text means, when the reader hovers, focuses or presses and holds it.

combineWith.how: An icon button has its name in aria-label and its consequence in data-tip.
A badge or a status chip says what its state means in its data-tip.
sednaUi.tips.gate turns the hints off while a guided tour owns the reader's attention.

useFor: The page an app shows instead of the one asked for: access denied, not found, a server error, an expired session or a maintenance window, and the warning before a session ends.

combineWith.how: Every page but not found is .auth-layout, as there is nothing to navigate to.
Not found keeps the frame, with its block at the top of .page.
Each page is one .empty-state--page: the code, the title, one line of why and the actions.
Each page has a drawing of its own, at .state-art--lg.
Not found puts the trail to the missing record at the top of .page.
The session warning is the app's own alertdialog, shown with ShowModalAsync.
The time left in the session warning is a countdown in the app's words.

useFor: A whole page to start from, in the app's frame: an overview, a list, a record, the forms that create and change one, search, settings, an account and sign-in.

combineWith.how: A recipe is the content of .page, in the frame taken once from Shell; sign-in is the content of .auth-layout.
Every recipe starts with a page head: the title, a line of purpose and the actions for the whole page.
A list page puts the toolbar between the page head and the table's card.
A list page's table sits in a card, with the pager after it.
A detail page, a list beside its record and settings lay their two regions out in a .sedna-split.
While a list loads it keeps its head and toolbar, and only its rows are skeletons.
A long create or edit form keeps its actions in reach.
